### kenithphilip/FedPy
- URL: https://github.com/kenithphilip/FedPy
- Exact commit / revision: `628fd0a536e49c8dfdba1d227cd4b1a87b89209f` (tree `d94c713746c4180851b6ecd576eb6e4b962d658c`)
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: Apache-2.0 FedRAMP 20x evidence stack with a read-only AWS/GCP/Kubernetes collector, coverage for the published 63 KSI / 223-requirement model, NIST 800-53 rollups, OSCAL Assessment Results, NIST-to-SOC2/ISO27001/HIPAA crosswalks, signed manifests, optional RFC 3161 timestamps, append-only run ledger, inventory/change/anomaly reports, ticket/SIEM/webhook integrations, and a local tracker for governance requirements.
- Rare or undernoticed value: This is unusually close to a sellable continuous-compliance evidence factory rather than a scanner. The repository includes both technical evidence collection and the governance-state layer, plus explicit read-only runtime guardrails and tamper-evident output.
- Likely buyer / user: SaaS/cloud providers pursuing FedRAMP 20x, defense contractors, 3PAO-adjacent consultants, compliance MSPs and cloud security teams.
- Painful problem: FedRAMP evidence is expensive to gather, normalize, crosswalk and refresh; static screenshots and spreadsheets become stale quickly.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price FedRAMP 20x evidence-readiness setup, then a managed weekly evidence-refresh service delivering signed evidence packs, drift deltas and remediation tickets before attempting full SaaS.
- Build-time / data advantage: Likely 4-8+ months of cloud-collector, standards, report, signing, inventory and tracker work compressed into one codebase.
- Concrete evidence inspected: exact signed latest commit; recursive tree with substantial `cloud-evidence/core`, cloud auth/provider, report, tracker and test surfaces; `cloud-evidence/core/readonly-guardrail.ts` blocks non-read AWS SDK operations before dispatch and layers retry/backoff; README documents 38 collector test files / 396 tests and 11 tracker test files / 99 tests, OSCAL outputs, signed manifests, RFC3161, run ledger and integrations.
- License / rights: Apache-2.0 root LICENSE verified at the exact revision; NOTICE present.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable subject to Apache-2.0/NOTICE obligations and third-party service/data terms.
- Why it is non-obvious: The repo name `FedPy` undersells a large TypeScript compliance platform and the valuable collector is nested under `cloud-evidence/`.
- Score: A 5 / B 5 / C 5 / D 5 / E 4 / F 5 = **29/30**. Revenue is immediate as a managed evidence service; evidence/completeness is 4 rather than 5 because this run verified source/tests/schema surfaces but did not execute a real customer cloud collection.
- Combination opportunities: Strongest current compliance cluster: FedPy collectors/signing -> Evidentia evidence/control plane -> FireDrill recovery proof -> Bernstein workflow/remediation orchestration. FedPy may replace much of the need for ad-hoc AWS/GCP collector work in the existing Attestful/Evidentia pilot.
- Next action: Run a synthetic AWS/GCP/K8s fixture through collection + offline verification, deliberately omit one required evidence path, tamper with one output, and confirm both failures remain non-pass before promoting to MASTER.

### defenseunicorns/lula
- URL: https://github.com/defenseunicorns/lula
- Exact commit / revision: `fc99c159365ca5d546aac88527d42614718024e2`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch
- What it contains: Apache-2.0 GitOps compliance manager: spreadsheet/eMASS import, YAML controls-as-code, control-to-source mappings, Git history, PR review, change-impact crawl, multi-framework control management and report/assessment export. It is the active successor to the OSCAL-centric Lula 1.
- Rare or undernoticed value: It makes control ownership and implementation narratives reviewable in normal Git workflows and can flag PRs that touch mapped compliance code. That is useful human-governance glue around automated evidence collectors.
- Likely buyer / user: security/compliance teams in engineering-led organizations, defense contractors and consultants moving spreadsheet controls into version control.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: compliance-repository conversion and managed control-change review service; migrate an existing spreadsheet/eMASS workbook into Git-native control files and monitor mapped code changes.
- Build-time / data advantage: 1-3 months saved on import/UI/history/mapping/change-impact plumbing.
- Concrete evidence inspected: active repo README at exact commit; command examples for PR crawl with UUID/SHA256 mappings; control YAML schema; web UI/import/export architecture; root Apache-2.0 LICENSE verified. README explicitly says Lula 1 is maintenance-only and explains why Lula 2 moved away from OSCAL-first workflows.
- License / rights: Apache-2.0.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable subject to Apache-2.0.
- Why it is non-obvious: The most valuable angle is not automated testing but compliance change-management embedded in PR workflows.
- Score: A 3 / B 4 / C 4 / D 3 / E 4 / F 5 = **23/30**. Strong implementation value, but weaker direct recurring evidence collection than FedPy/Evidentia.
- Combination opportunities: Use Lula as the human control/mapping/change-review front end while FedPy/Evidentia supply recurring machine evidence and FireDrill supplies recovery proof.
- Next action: Test whether a FedPy/Evidentia evidence reference can be linked cleanly to Lula control mappings without duplicating the system of record.

### kirilurbonas/FireDrill
- URL: https://github.com/kirilurbonas/FireDrill
- Exact commit / revision: `1e532b17e49e4424f988b29dd338ae6c48dc20f3` (tree `7f7b552966f5e25042aed877a580e490206e2e5a`)
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: Apache-2.0 backup-agnostic recovery verification for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and Velero/Kubernetes namespaces. It provisions disposable Docker/Kubernetes sandboxes, restores real backups, measures RTO/RPO, runs checksums/canaries/custom queries, then emits signed JSON plus detached Ed25519 and in-toto/DSSE evidence. It also exports control matrices, tracks RTO history and has CI/Kubernetes operator modes.
- Rare or undernoticed value: It directly closes two gaps in the current Recovery Evidence Gate thesis: cryptographic evidence integrity and **evidence expiry**. `firedrill gate --max-age --require-signed` fails builds when named drills have no evidence, evidence is stale, or signatures do not meet policy; the tool also supports signer-key pinning.
- Likely buyer / user: regulated SaaS, platform/SRE teams, MSPs, cyber-resilience programs, Kubernetes operators and audit/compliance teams.
- Painful problem: backup jobs can report success while recovery is broken; even a past successful drill becomes meaningless if it silently stops running.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: managed recovery-proof service: install/configure drills, run them on customer cadence, retain signed evidence, alert on RTO/RPO failures and optionally enforce a deployment gate. Price per protected workload/environment plus onboarding.
- Build-time / data advantage: 4-6+ months saved on multi-engine restore drivers, sandboxing, encrypted/compressed source handling, evidence signing/attestation, freshness gates, operator/CI integration and reports.
- Concrete evidence inspected: exact latest commit; Apache-2.0 LICENSE; substantial tree with CLI, docs, CI/release, GitHub Action, RecoveryDrill CRD/operator, Grafana dashboard and examples for Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB/Velero. README documents Ed25519 evidence, DSSE/in-toto attestations, cosign verification, ransomware canary, per-control evidence matrix, stale/missing-evidence gate, history trends, K8s isolation and encrypted backup handling.
- License / rights: Apache-2.0 verified at exact revision.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable subject to Apache-2.0 obligations.
- Why it is non-obvious: A backup-drill CLI quietly contains a near-complete cryptographic recovery-evidence control plane, including the freshness gate that many compliance tools omit.
- Score: A 5 / B 5 / C 5 / D 5 / E 4 / F 5 = **29/30**. Evidence/completeness is 4 only because this run source-inspected rather than executing the integrations.
- Combination opportunities: FireDrill should become the preferred recovery-proof worker beneath Evidentia/FedPy. Feed signed drill evidence into control mapping; use Bernstein for conditional remediation/escalation; compare against existing restore-drill only where its provider coverage is better.
- Next action: Synthetic kill-or-advance benchmark: successful restore, corrupted content/canary, stale evidence, missing evidence, tampered JSON, wrong signer key, RTO miss and RPO miss. If every negative case fails closed, promote to MASTER and use it for the paid compliance/recovery pilot.

### sipyourdrink-ltd/bernstein
- URL: https://github.com/sipyourdrink-ltd/bernstein
- Exact commit / revision: `a882b6f6f06db24516624f4a4b399ef07669d52f`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong
- What it contains: Apache-2.0 deterministic workflow/orchestration layer for governed AI/automation runs with replay journal, lineage, optional HMAC-chained audit log, signed run receipts and artifact contracts. It ships an `audit-evidence-pack` workflow that scopes evidence, fans out collectors, assembles a pack, runs a mock-auditor stage, conditionally loops through remediation and then signs/delivers the result.
- Rare or undernoticed value: The useful piece is not another agent framework; it is a reproducible evidence/remediation workflow engine with conditional gates and signed receipts. Its OSCAL module generates NIST OSCAL 1.1.0 Assessment Results from audit-chain/lineage evidence and validates output against a vendored schema.
- Likely buyer / user: compliance MSPs, security teams, GRC automation vendors and regulated engineering organizations that need repeatable evidence collection/remediation runs.
- Painful problem: Evidence collection often ends in a human spreadsheet loop; failures are found late and remediation is tracked separately from the evidence run.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: managed monthly/quarterly evidence runbook: connect existing collectors, execute a deterministic evidence graph, route failed checks to remediation, obtain approval where needed and deliver a signed evidence packet.
- Build-time / data advantage: 2-4 months saved on workflow graph/replay, lineage, artifact contracts, conditional remediation, receipts and OSCAL emission.
- Concrete evidence inspected: exact signed latest commit; README workflow/receipt/audit-chain documentation; root Apache-2.0 LICENSE; `src/bernstein/compliance/oscal.py` emits OSCAL Assessment Results, carries content/parent hashes and HMAC prefix references into observations, supports a `since` lower bound and schema-validates output. Limitation: current control-domain mapping is resource-type-derived and should not be treated as authoritative framework mapping without hardening.
- License / rights: Apache-2.0 verified at exact revision.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable subject to Apache-2.0; external integrations keep their own terms.
- Why it is non-obvious: The compliance value is buried inside a broader AI-agent governance/orchestration repo; repository naming gives no hint that it contains an audit-evidence workflow and OSCAL emitter.
- Score: A 4 / B 4 / C 5 / D 5 / E 4 / F 5 = **27/30**. Strong workflow substrate, with evidence score held at 4 because current control mapping semantics are not yet authoritative.
- Combination opportunities: FedPy/Attestful collectors -> Bernstein deterministic workflow + remediation/approval -> Evidentia control/evidence plane -> FireDrill signed recovery proof. This turns the current cluster into an actual managed recurring service before a dedicated SaaS UI exists.
- Next action: Wire two synthetic collectors plus FireDrill-style restore evidence into `audit-evidence-pack`; inject one missing item and one failed recovery proof; require remediation/approval before the final receipt can be issued.
